title: Abhinav Seva Sansthan Mahavidyalaya v. U.P. Power Corporation Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
coram: Sunil Ambwani, J. & Kashi Nath Pandey, J.
disposition: Writ petition dismissed (liberty to appeal the final assessment)
headnote: Where a consumer has paid compounding charges for meter tampering / theft of electricity under Section 152 of the Electricity Act, 2003, the tampering stands compounded and the licensee need not follow the meter sealing/testing procedure of para 5.6(d) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the assessment can stand. Section 152 operates at two stages: under sub-section (2), where no prosecution has yet been instituted, payment of the compounding sum sets the person at liberty and bars proceedings; sub-section (3) (acceptance deemed an acquittal) applies only where a prosecution is already pending. Compounding therefore does not require a pending prosecution. A compounding amount paid without protest or contemporaneous objection cannot later be assailed as realised under coercion.

holding_units.topic: Meter-testing procedure vs a compounded theft offence
holding_units.question: Where a consumer has paid compounding charges under Section 152 for meter tampering, must the licensee still follow the meter sealing/testing procedure under para 5.6(d) of the Supply Code before the compounding/assessment can stand?
holding_units.holding: No. Once the sum is paid under Section 152(1) and the offence is deemed compounded, the tampering stands admitted-compounded and the question of following the meter-testing procedure (para 5.6(d)) does not arise. The theft assessment was made on the Code's formula (Annexure 6.3); the procedural challenge fails.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Contracted load 7.5 KW against 32 KW connected; meter found tampered (a shunt resistance reducing the recording by 50%), the inspection videographed; the petitioner paid the compounding charge (Rs. 3,20,000) and part of the provisional assessment voluntarily, without protest.
holding_units.qualifier: The correctness of the provisional assessment (Rs. 4,29,359.56) was left to the statutory appeal under Section 127.

holding_units.topic: Compounding of electricity theft — whether a pending prosecution is required
holding_units.holding: Section 152(2) and (3) operate at different stages: under s.152(2), where no criminal proceeding has yet been instituted, payment of the compounding sum sets the person at liberty and bars institution of proceedings; s.152(3) (acceptance deemed an acquittal) applies only where a prosecution is already pending. Compounding therefore does not require a pending prosecution.
holding_units.flag: The judgment refers throughout to 'Section 152(2) of the Electricity Supply Code 2005'; Section 152 is in the Electricity Act, 2003. Recorded, not merged.

principle_tags.application: A compounding/assessment amount paid without protest or contemporaneous objection cannot later be assailed as realised under coercion.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the provisional theft assessment
not_decided.note: The quantum of the provisional electricity-theft assessment was not adjudicated; liberty was granted to pursue the statutory appeal under Section 127.

authorities.name: Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors. v. Megh Raj
authorities.proposition: The power to compound under Section 152 presupposes a pending prosecution, acceptance of the sum amounting to an acquittal.
authorities.how_treated: Distinguished / confined — read as applicable only to compounding under s.152(3), where a prosecution is pending; it does not govern s.152(2) compounding before any prosecution is instituted.
